Let me analyze this OIML certificate markdown.

- Address lines: Thijsseweg 11, 2629 JA Delft, the Netherlands

- Phone: +31 88 636 2332

Certified type:
- Category: "Automatic level gauge" — recommendation R85 "Automatic level gauges for measuring the level of liquid in stationary storage tanks". Category per examples: "Automatic level gauge".
- Type designations: ["CS-MI"]
- Description: "An automatic level gauge (ALG) with temperature and density displacer sensor" — note OCR says "senor" — I'll keep as "sensor"? Don't fabricate — but OCR typo; I'll write "sensor" as reasonable correction. Actually rule says don't fabricate; correcting an obvious OCR typo should be fine.
- Manufacturers mark: Aubon

Recommendation:
- id: "R85-1&2"? The certificate says R 85-1&2: 2008. Canonical id — probably "R85". The recommendation is R 85 (parts 1&2), edition 2008. Hmm. The schema says id canonical e.g. "R60" not "OIML R 60". Edition (int): 2008. The cert says "R 85-1&2: 2008". So id: "R85", edition: 2008, maybe amendment: null, scheme: "A", accuracy_classes: [] (not mentioned).

Actually, is "R85-1&2" the id? I'd say canonical id "R85", with edition 2008. Maybe note parts in id as "R85-1&2"? The rule says canonical like "R60". R85 has parts 1 and 2 issued 2008. I'll use "R85-1&2" — hmm, that could break lookups. Safer: "R85". But the certificate title says "R 85-1&2: 2008". I'll use id "R85-1&2"? The example converts "OIML R 60" to "R60". For "R 85-1&2" the natural canonical is "R85-1&2". Hmm. Many databases use "R85". I'll go with "R85-1&2" to preserve the parts info? The rule is about removing "OIML " prefix, not about merging parts. "R 85-1&2: 2008" → "R85-1&2". I'll use "R85-1&2". Actually let me think: canonicalization "R60" not "OIML R 60" — the transformation removes the prefix. So "R 85-1&2" → "R85-1&2". Yes, keep parts.

Edition: 2008 (int).

Test reports:
- No. NMi-3806928-01, dated 7 April 2026, 36 pages, role: type_evaluation_report (it says "OIML Type Evaluation Report" and report includes tests). The footnote says "In type evaluation report NMi-3806928-01...". So role: "type_evaluation_report".

Documentation file: "Documentation folder no. R85-2008-A-NL1-26.01-1" — role: documentation_file. id: "R85-2008-A-NL1-26.01-1". No date/pages.

Characteristics (Table 1):
- Maximum measuring range level: 55 metres → maximum_measuring_range_level, value 55, unit "m" (metres). unit_symbol: "m".
- Ambient temperature range: -40 – +70 °C; condensing humidity → value {min: -40, max: 70}, unit °C, plus a separate note "condensing humidity". Could add characteristic ambient_conditions: "condensing humidity"? Better: add a separate type-level characteristic "ambient_humidity": {value: "condensing humidity"}. Or include in description. I'll add `ambient_humidity` as string value "condensing humidity".

- Displacer types (config/components):
  - LF1 and LF13: without additional sensor
  - VTM-I: including temperature sensor
  - DSM-CS: including temperature and density sensors

These are components! Displacers LF1, LF13, VTM-I, DSM-CS. The certified type CS-MI is an ALG with temperature and density displacer sensors. Components with role "displacer":
- type_designations ["LF1", "LF13"], characteristics: {additional_sensors: "none"}
- type_designations ["VTM-I"], characteristics: {includes temperature sensor}
- type_designations ["DSM-CS"], characteristics: {includes temperature and density sensors}

Hmm, alternatives "OR" — the instrument can be equipped with any of these displacer types. So alternatives: "OR" for the group? The schema has components[] each with role, type_designations, alternatives, characteristics. I could do a single component entry role "displacer" with type_designations ["LF1","LF13","VTM-I","DSM-CS"] and alternatives "OR", with per-type characteristics... but characteristics is a single object. Better: three component entries (grouping by sensor configuration):
1. role: "displacer", type_designations: ["LF1", "LF13"], alternatives: "OR", characteristics: {sensor_configuration: "without additional sensor"}? Hmm "alternatives" within this entry means LF1 OR LF13. Between entries, they're also alternatives. I'll structure:
- component 1: role "displacer", type_designations ["LF1","LF13"], alternatives "OR", characteristics {additional_sensors: {value: "none"}}
- component 2: role "displacer", type_designations ["VTM-I"], alternatives "OR", characteristics {additional_sensors: {value: "temperature sensor"}}
- component 3: role "displacer", type_designations ["DSM-CS"], alternatives "OR", characteristics {additional_sensors: {value: "temperature and density sensors"}}

Actually cleaner: characteristics as structured values? The schema says characteristics{} — for components, could be simple. I'll use structured values to be safe: {"sensors_included": {"value": "none", "unit_symbol": null, "unit_id": null}}.

Hmm, but maybe simpler to put displacer types into config_level characteristics. But components seem right since these are named sub-assemblies (displacers with software versions!). Actually the software identification table lists "VTM-I Floater" and "DSM-CS Floater" with SW versions — these are software of the components.

- Temperature displacer measuring range: two config-dependent values:
  - -5 – +35 °C for VTM-I displacer
  - -45 – +75 °C for DSM-CS displacer
  → config_level: attribute "temperature_displacer_measuring_range", axis "displacer_type", values: [{condition: "VTM-I", value: {min:-5,max:35}, unit "°C"}, {condition: "DSM-CS", value: {min:-45,max:75}, unit "°C"}]

- Density displacer measuring range: 600 – 1100 kg/m³ at maximum viscosity of 15 mPa.s (only applicable for DSM-CS). → config_level or type_level with footnote-like condition. Since only applicable to DSM-CS, it's config-dependent:
  config_level: attribute "density_displacer_measuring_range", axis "displacer_type", values: [{condition: "DSM-CS", value: {min:600, max:1100}, unit_symbol: "kg/m³"}]. And add characteristic maximum_viscosity: 15 mPa.s (condition DSM-CS). I could add another config_level entry "maximum_viscosity": {condition: "DSM-CS", value: 15, unit_symbol: "mPa·s"}. Or keep viscosity note in description. I'll add config_level for viscosity too.

- Power supply voltage: "220 V AC @ 50/60Hz or 20 – 60 V DC". This is an OR of two options:
  Option 1: 220 V AC, 50/60 Hz
  Option 2: 20–60 V DC
  → config_level with axis "power_supply_option"? Or split type_level:
  - power_supply_voltage_ac: 220 V (option 1)
  - power_supply_frequency: {min:50, max:60} Hz (AC)
  - power_supply_voltage_dc: {min:20, max:60} V (option 2)
  - power_supply_type: ["AC", "DC"] — hmm.
  
  I think config_level is cleanest:
  attribute "power_supply_voltage", axis "power_supply_type":
  - {condition: "AC", value: 220, unit_symbol: "V"}
  - {condition: "DC", value: {min: 20, max: 60}, unit_symbol: "V"}
  attribute "power_supply_frequency", axis "power_supply_type":
  - {condition: "AC", value: {min: 50, max: 60}, unit_symbol: "Hz"}
  And type_level power_supply_type: {value: "AC or DC"}? Hmm, maybe config-level handles it. I'll do:
  config_level entries:
  1. {attribute: "power_supply_voltage", axis: "power_supply_type", values: [{condition: "AC", value: 220, unit_symbol: "V"}, {condition: "DC", value: {min:20, max:60}, unit_symbol: "V"}]}
  2. {attribute: "power_supply_frequency", axis: "power_supply_type", values: [{condition: "AC", value: {min:50, max:60}, unit_symbol: "Hz"}]}

  For AC "220 V AC" — is 220 single value or range? Nominal 220 V. Value: 220.

- Software identification — this is a matrix table (matrix_tables):
  columns: component, sw_version, crc_checksum
  rows:
  - Main Control Board: V1.01675, 11123
  - Display Board: 2076, 42800
  - VTM-I Floater: 1.53, 27251
  - DSM-CS Floater: 1.0, 19977

  Note "V1.01675" — hmm, that might be "V1.01" + something? OCR shows "V1.01675" and CRC 11123. Probably SW version "V1.01675"? Could be "V1.0167" + "5"? Keep as given: "V1.01675". Display Board SW version "2076"? That seems odd but keep as string.

  matrix_tables entry: name "Software identification", columns ["component", "sw_version", "crc_checksum"], rows as above. Values as strings (versions).

- Data communication:
  Inputs: HART communication, RS485 communication
  Outputs: RS485 interface with transmission protocol; HART communication; Digital Output K1 (not for legal metrology); Digital Output K2 (not for legal metrology); 4-20 mA Output (not for legal metrology)
  Transmission protocols: Modbus protocol; GPU protocol
  
  These are descriptive. Could put in type_level characteristics as string values (lists). E.g.:
  - data_communication_inputs: {value: ["HART", "RS485"]}? Value must be number, {min,max}, or string. Lists not allowed per schema. So use strings: "HART communication; RS485 communication". Or add matrix table. I'll use string values joined with "; ".

Footnotes:
- Marker "1)": "In type evaluation report NMi-3806928-01 annex 4 includes performance test on the displacer for liquid density and temperature. The maximum permissible error is based on OIML R117-1:2019."
  The superscript ¹ is attached to the report number on page 2. No characteristic value references it directly, but include in footnotes[].

Model family: Is there more than one model variant? The type is CS-MI, single type with different displacer configurations. Not really a model family — it's one model with configuration axes. I'll omit model_family (or include with single model?). Schema says include ONLY if cert covers >1 model variant. The displacer types are more like configurations/components. I'll omit model_family.

Date issued: 7 April 2026. ISO format? Schema just says date_issued. I'll use "2026-04-07". Hmm, or keep raw "7 April 2026". I'll use ISO "2026-04-07" for consistency. Test report date: "2026-04-07".
